reason: The text focuses on Job, who is explicitly portrayed as exceptional and extraordinary—'the greatest man among all the people of the East' (וַיְהִי הָאִישׁ הַהוּא גָדוֹל מִכָּל־בְּנֵי־קֶדֶם), renowned for his perfect righteousness (תָּם וְיָשָׁר). He is not a 'regular person' but rather a paradigmatic figure of exceptional virtue and divine favor. His children and servants are barely characterized and serve primarily as supporting figures in his narrative rather than as examples of how 'regular people' are portrayed. The passage emphasizes Job's singularity and exceptional status, not the favorable treatment of ordinary people.
